name: Keyva
about: Ten reels for keyva.ae, Dubai property research built on Dubai Land Department records (batch 3, 26 Oct 2026).

lines.text: There's no JVC in Dubai's rent records.
It's filed as Al Barsha South Fourth.
Dubai Marina? Marsa Dubai.
JLT? Al Thanyah Fifth.
Dubai Hills? Hadaeq Sheikh Mohammed Bin Rashid.
And Downtown is filed as Burj Khalifa.
Keyva matches the name you know to the name on record, so the numbers add up.
Buying in Dubai from India? There's a quarter million dollar limit.
Each resident can send up to two hundred and fifty thousand dollars a financial year, all purposes combined.
captions: two hundred and fifty thousand dollars

lines.text: But co-owners can each send their own. Four family members on the title: up to a million dollars.
Past ten lakh rupees, your bank collects twenty percent tax at source. It's credited against your tax, not a cost.
Keyva's India guide puts a source and a date on every rule.
Buying a home in Dubai? There's a knowledge fee.
Ten dirhams. And a ten dirham innovation fee.
Two hundred and fifty for the title deed, and two hundred and fifty for the map.
Taking a mortgage? The title deed, knowledge and innovation fees come twice: once for the sale, once for the mortgage.
Small, but they add up. Keyva lists every fee, and who sets it.
Most price tools always give you a number. Keyva sometimes won't.
Fewer than eight comparable sales? A fair price would be guesswork, so it says so.
Early in a month, this month can mean two days of sales. In Dubai Marina, twenty-two.
So Keyva uses the last thirty days, and shows the count on every figure.
Buying off-plan in Dubai? Your money shouldn't go to the developer directly.
By law, every project gets its own escrow account, used only to build it, and protected from the developer's creditors.
Keyva's project check shows what the register holds: the status, the escrow bank, the developer's licence, and the completion target.
What it can't check, like whether the account is funded, it tells you.
Your landlord wants more rent? Check the date on the notice first.
A landlord must give ninety days' written notice before changing any term of your contract, rent included.
Served late, an otherwise lawful increase doesn't bind you for that renewal.
Keyva's rent check shows the legal cap, and the notice rule, side by side.
That car loan could shrink your Dubai mortgage.
The Central Bank caps all your loan repayments together at half your income.
Earn thirty thousand a month? That's fifteen thousand, for every loan you have.
A three thousand car loan leaves twelve thousand for the mortgage. That's a fifth less to borrow against.
Keyva's mortgage calculator counts your existing debts, against the Central Bank's caps.
That ten percent deposit? It's not a law.
It's a market custom, agreed between buyer and seller.
No government document sets the percentage.
What is official: Contract F, made by a registered broker in Dubai REST. It records the price, the payment plan, and who pays the transfer fee.
Keyva marks what's law, and what's custom.
A Dubai property ad with no permit number? That's the biggest red flag.
Every legitimate ad must carry a Trakheesi permit from the Land Department.
Scan its QR code in the Dubai REST app. It confirms the permit is real, active, and for this property.
But a valid permit doesn't mean a fair price.
For that, check what similar homes actually sold for, on Keyva.
Dubai publishes what homes actually sell for.
Not asking prices. Registered sales, from the Land Department's open data.
A listing only shows you what's asked.
Keyva turns those records into typical prices, area by area, with the number of sales and the date on every figure.
Check before you offer.
